title: “448_Project_Stroke_Data” author: “Anurag Nepal” date: “2025-03-16” output: pdf_document: default html_document: df_print: paged

Stroke Data Analysis: Key Insights

Healthcare Dataset (SFSU MATH 448 Project)

Main Findings

  • Data Imbalance: Only about 5% of patients in the dataset had a stroke, requiring special handling (e.g., SMOTE) for modeling.
  • Age: Stroke risk increases with age. Seniors and middle-aged groups show higher stroke rates.
  • Glucose & BMI: Higher average glucose levels and BMI are associated with increased stroke risk.
  • Gender: Stroke rates are similar across genders, but distribution varies slightly.
  • Smoking Status: Former smokers have a higher stroke rate than current or never smokers.
  • Heart Disease & Hypertension: Both conditions significantly increase stroke risk.
  • Work Type & Residence: Some work types and urban/rural residence show different risk patterns.
  • Modeling: Random Forest and Boosting models (with SMOTE) achieved the best balance of sensitivity and specificity. QDA was unstable due to data rank issues.
  • Missing Data: BMI missing values were imputed using group means by age and gender.

See below for detailed code, plots, and model results.

na_counts = colSums(is.na(stroke_data))

stroke_data = stroke_data[stroke_data$gender != "Other", ]
categorize_age = function(age) {
  if (age >= 0 & age <= 1) {
    return('Infant')
  } else if (age > 1 & age <= 12) {
    return('Children')
  } else if (age > 12 & age < 20) {
    return('Teenager')
  } else if (age >= 20 & age <= 39) {
    return('Adult')
  } else if (age > 39 & age <= 59) {
    return('Middle Aged')
  } else {
    return('Senior')
  }
}

stroke_data$age_group = sapply(stroke_data$age, categorize_age)
unique(stroke_data$age_group)

colnames(avg_bmi_by_group) = c("age_group","gender","avg_bmi")

stroke_data = stroke_data %>%
  select(-id, -age_group,-Residence_type,-gender) %>%
  mutate(
    ever_married = as.factor(ever_married),
    work_type = as.factor(work_type),
    smoking_status = as.factor(smoking_status),
    hypertension = as.factor(hypertension),
    heart_disease = as.factor(heart_disease),
    stroke = as.factor(stroke)
  )
stroke_data = stroke_data %>%
  mutate(stroke = factor(stroke, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("YES", "NO")))
set.seed(123)  
trainIndex = createDataPartition(stroke_data$stroke, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train_data = stroke_data[trainIndex, ]
test_data = stroke_data[-trainIndex, ]
prop.table(table(train_data$stroke))
## 
##        YES         NO 
## 0.04892368 0.95107632
prop.table(table(test_data$stroke))
## 
##        YES         NO 
## 0.04830287 0.95169713

Define Training Controls

We’ll define two trainControl objects for 5-fold cross-validation: one without SMOTE and one with SMOTE for class balancing. We’ll use these across all models and scenarios.

# Without SMOTE
ctrl_base = trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  classProbs = TRUE,           
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,  
)

ctrl_smote = trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  sampling = "smote"           
)

For each model (Logistic Regression, LDA, QDA, KNN), we’ll train under four scenarios: 1. No SMOTE, No PCA 2. SMOTE, No PCA 3. No SMOTE, PCA 4. SMOTE, PCA

Logistic Regression

# No SMOTE, No PCA
set.seed(123)
logit_no_smote_no_pca = train(
  stroke ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "glm", 
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = ctrl_base, 
  metric = "ROC"
)
logit_pred_no_smote_no_pca_prob = predict(logit_no_smote_no_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")
logit_pred_no_smote_no_pca_class = predict(logit_no_smote_no_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
roc_logit_no_smote_no_pca = roc(test_data$stroke, logit_pred_no_smote_no_pca_prob[,"YES"])
## Setting levels: control = YES, case = NO
## Setting direction: controls > cases
acc_logit_no_smote_no_pca = confusionMatrix(logit_pred_no_smote_no_pca_class, test_data$stroke)$overall["Accuracy"]


# SMOTE, No PCA
set.seed(123)
logit_smote_no_pca = train(
  stroke ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "glm", 
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = ctrl_smote, 
  metric = "ROC"
)
## Loading required package: recipes

logit_pred_smote_no_pca_prob = predict(logit_smote_no_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")
logit_pred_smote_no_pca_class = predict(logit_smote_no_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
roc_logit_smote_no_pca = roc(test_data$stroke, logit_pred_smote_no_pca_prob[,"YES"])
## Setting levels: control = YES, case = NO
## Setting direction: controls > cases
acc_logit_smote_no_pca = confusionMatrix(logit_pred_smote_no_pca_class, test_data$stroke)$overall["Accuracy"]


# No SMOTE, PCA
set.seed(123)
logit_no_smote_pca = train(
  stroke ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "glm", 
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = ctrl_base, 
  preProcess = c("center", "scale", "pca"),  # PCA with centering and scaling
  metric = "ROC"
)
## Warning: glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred
logit_pred_no_smote_pca_prob = predict(logit_no_smote_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")
logit_pred_no_smote_pca_class = predict(logit_no_smote_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
roc_logit_no_smote_pca = roc(test_data$stroke, logit_pred_no_smote_pca_prob[,"YES"])
## Setting levels: control = YES, case = NO
## Setting direction: controls > cases
acc_logit_no_smote_pca = confusionMatrix(logit_pred_no_smote_pca_class, test_data$stroke)$overall["Accuracy"]

# SMOTE, PCA
set.seed(123)
logit_smote_pca = train(
  stroke ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "glm", 
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = ctrl_smote, 
  preProcess = c("center", "scale", "pca"),
  metric = "ROC"
)
## Warning: glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred
logit_pred_smote_pca_prob = predict(logit_smote_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")
roc_logit_smote_pca = roc(test_data$stroke, logit_pred_smote_pca_prob[,"YES"])
## Setting levels: control = YES, case = NO
## Setting direction: controls > cases
logit_pred_smote_pca_class = predict(logit_smote_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
acc_logit_smote_pca = confusionMatrix(logit_pred_smote_pca_class, test_data$stroke)$overall["Accuracy"]

# Plot ROC curves
plot(roc_logit_no_smote_no_pca, col = "blue", main = "ROC for Logistic Regression")
lines(roc_logit_smote_no_pca, col = "red")
lines(roc_logit_no_smote_pca, col = "green")
lines(roc_logit_smote_pca, col = "purple")
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c("No SMOTE No PCA", "SMOTE No PCA", "No SMOTE PCA", "SMOTE PCA"), 
       col = c("blue", "red", "green", "purple"), 
       lty = 1)

### Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA)

# No SMOTE, No PCA
set.seed(123)
qda_no_smote_no_pca = tryCatch({
  train(
    stroke ~ ., 
    data = train_data, 
    method = "qda",
    trControl = ctrl_base,

acc_boost_no_smote_no_pca = confusionMatrix(boost_pred_no_smote_no_pca_class, test_data$stroke)$overall["Accuracy"]

# SMOTE, No PCA
set.seed(123)
boost_smote_no_pca = train(
  stroke ~ ., 
  data = train_data, 
  method = "gbm",
  trControl = ctrl_smote, 
  tuneLength = 3,
  metric = "ROC",
  verbose = FALSE
)
boost_pred_smote_no_pca = predict(boost_smote_no_pca, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")

## Setting levels: control = YES, case = NO

Because the QDA model fails to fit in every fold due to the rank deficiency issue, no predictions are produced. Without predictions, the performance metrics (like ROC) cannot be computed, leading to the “missing values” warning.
